title: rust/lichen-schc/src/context.rs: MSB matching panics when shift equals u128 bit width
description:
In rule_matches(), when Mo::Msb is used with mo_arg = 0 and fd.length_bits = 128 (a full IPv6 address), the calculation `shift = fd.length_bits - mo_arg` yields 128. The subsequent `val >> shift` panics in debug builds because shifting a u128 by 128 bits is an overflow. The guard on line 184 only rejects mo_arg > length_bits, not the case where shift >= 128.

Fix suggestion: Add an early-out check: `if mo_arg == 0 { /* comparing 0 MSBs always matches */ }` before the shift, or clamp shift to 127 max. Alternatively, use wrapping_shr or checked_shr to avoid the panic.

File: rust/lichen-schc/src/context.rs
Line: 188
Category: correctness
resolution: Already fixed. In rust/lichen-schc/src/context.rs lines 246-248, the MSB matching code handles mo_arg == 0 with continue to skip the shift operation, preventing the u128 shift-by-128 panic. Test msb_matching_handles_full_width_boundaries (lines 554-626) explicitly covers this case with length_bits=128 and mo_arg=0.
